name: blessed-practices
description: Blessed code practices, one installable skill per practice — layering, domain modelling, dependency hygiene, comment discipline, and how an agent should push back

plugins.name: comments-describe-the-code
plugins.description: Comments describe the code itself, not the prompt or conversation that produced it — and a long justifying comment is a code smell pointing at the code

plugins.name: dependencies
plugins.description: Manage dependencies with the ecosystem's package manager; never hand-edit the manifest

plugins.name: diminishing-returns
plugins.description: Pursue the highest-value work first and stop when the expected value of the next improvement no longer justifies its full cost

plugins.name: design-with-known-limits
plugins.description: Design systems with explicit correctness limits, failure modes, and operational assumptions instead of automatically engineering every weakness away

plugins.name: domain-modelling
plugins.description: What goes inside the core — ubiquitous language, aggregates as consistency boundaries, entities and values, illegal states unrepresentable, where behaviour lives, persistence ignorance, events versus effects, bounded contexts

plugins.name: fix-the-assumption-not-the-hack
plugins.description: When a feature invalidates an assumption the design rests on, rethink the pattern instead of landing a tweaky hack

plugins.name: idiomatic-by-default
plugins.description: Take the ecosystem's standard path unless there is an articulable reason not to, and don't escalate decisions an idiom already answers

plugins.name: illegal-states-unrepresentable
plugins.description: Model data so invalid combinations cannot be constructed — use variants, precise values and boundary parsing instead of optionals plus runtime assertions

plugins.name: layering
plugins.description: Where code goes and which way its dependencies point — inward-pointing dependencies, what each layer owns, what may cross a boundary, ports and adapters

plugins.name: modular-and-layered-code
plugins.description: Architect so a future agent can act at a single layer — strict tested contracts, boundary-focused testing, pure logic separated from I/O, impurity confined to the edges

plugins.name: push-back-and-verify-assumptions
plugins.description: Treat the operator as a fellow engineer — push back on wrong premises, state assumptions explicitly, and stop rather than build something plausibly correct

plugins.name: write-the-present-not-the-diff
plugins.description: Prose states what is true now — not the claim it replaced, the measurement that disproved it, or the path that got there
